assessments.reasoning: AGPL [28300,28765) supplies the trigger, beneficiaries, version, prominence, network-server access, price and copying method. Its terms resolve the paid-path and obscure-offer cases even where the correct source exists.

AGPL [3327,3594) defines modification by copying from or adapting some or all of a work in a way that requires copyright permission, with an exception for an exact copy. Deploying an exact copy therefore cannot alone establish the modification premise.

AGPL [5264,6955) ties object-code Corresponding Source to what is needed to generate, install, run an executable, and modify the work, including controlling scripts, subject to enumerated exclusions and automatically regenerable material. For a source-form work it is the work itself. An upstream archive missing the deployed changes fails this test even when freely downloadable.

limitations: Applying the rule requires evidence of modification, supported interaction, the users reached by the offer, and the contents and accessibility of the source. A download of the Program raises a separate conveyance question.
reasoning: AGPLv3 §13 requires the licensee's modified version, if it supports remote interaction through a computer network, to give every user interacting with it that way a prominent opportunity to obtain that version's Corresponding Source. The source must be accessible free of charge from a network server by a standard or customary means of copying software.
